subject.title: refactor(zalouser): compile blocks from CommonMark IR

question: Should ZaloUser consume parser block metadata through a supported plugin-SDK API, or should maintainers explicitly accept and own a bundled-only internal metadata facade?
rationale: The implementation is technically focused and proof-backed, but choosing whether hidden parser fields are a supported cross-package contract determines the long-term plugin architecture and compatibility obligation.

options.title: Add a narrow SDK capability
options.body: Expose only the block/list metadata needed by channel formatters through a documented, typed plugin-SDK surface with focused compatibility coverage.

options.title: Approve a bundled-only facade
options.body: Keep the metadata non-public, but establish a named internal facade and ownership tests so markdown-core changes cannot silently break ZaloUser.

options.title: Pause the refactor
options.body: Retain the existing ZaloUser scanner until maintainers choose the durable parser-to-plugin contract.

recommendation.title: Add a narrow SDK capability
recommendation.body: Expose only the block/list metadata needed by channel formatters through a documented, typed plugin-SDK surface with focused compatibility coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history ties this contributor directly to both sides of the proposed metadata boundary; an additional core/plugin-SDK owner should confirm the architectural choice.
